title: RemotiveBroker meta database json format schema
description: A meta database extends a conventional signal database with what that format cannot express: end-to-end protection, secure onboard communication, and the fill byte for unused bits. It works for `.ldf` and `.dbc`. The broker reads one when it has the database's own file name with `.meta.json` appended, so `./my_db.dbc` pairs with `./my_db.dbc.meta.json`. A sidecar does not name this schema; it states `formatVersion`, and a reader knows which schema that is.

formatVersion.description: File format version. Verifies that the RemotiveBroker can read the file.

description.description: What the file is for, in the author's words. Read and ignored.

frames.description: Frame names to the meta database information for that frame. A name must match a frame in the parent signal database.

e2e.description: End-to-end protection over the whole payload. It means the same as a group whose range is every byte of the frame, so the CRC and counter signals sit inside the protected area and the CRC covers the frame from its first byte.

groups.description: Protected parts of the payload, each a range of bytes.

unusedBitPattern.description: Value of a single byte, given as a decimal integer, used to fill the frame's unused bits. It covers the whole payload, protected areas included.

group.description: One protected part of a payload. `e2e` and `secoc` sit beside `range`, not inside it.

range.description: A part of a payload, in bytes.

offset.description: Byte offset inside the frame where this group starts.

size.description: Size of the group in bytes.

e2e.description: End-to-end protection over an area of a payload. Each profile needs its own fields; see `profile`.

profile.description: Which AUTOSAR profile protects the area. `PROFILE_AR_01A`, `01B`, `01C` and `01_LOW` are the four data id modes of profile 1 and require `dataId`. `PROFILE_AR_05` requires `dataId`. `PROFILE_AR_02` requires `dataIds`.

dataId.description: Data ID to be used in CRC calculation.

dataIds.description: The data ids of profile 2, one per value of its four-bit counter, so sixteen of them.

crc.description: Name of the signal containing the E2E checksum.

counter.description: Name of the signal containing the E2E counter.

secoc.description: Secure onboard communication over a group. All lengths are in bytes. The encoder lays a group out as authentic data, then the truncated freshness value, then the truncated authenticator, so the two truncated lengths have to fit inside the group.

dataId.description: Data ID mixed into the authenticator, unique per PDU.

authenticatorTruncLength.description: How many bytes of the authenticator are transmitted, taken from its most-significant end.

freshnessValueLength.description: How long the full freshness value is, the value the authenticator is computed over.

freshnessValueTruncLength.description: How many bytes of the freshness value are transmitted. Never more than `freshnessValueLength`.

timeDiff.description: Present in some databases and ignored by the broker.
